reward_breakdown.formula: browser gated by committed-state restart durability

criteria.name: seeded_login_and_session_isolation
criteria.description: Feature metadata: feature=auth_session; sub_feature=login_and_tab_isolation; kind=hard_gate; depends_on=none. This criterion is all-or-nothing. Open two ordinary tabs in the same browser context; do not use separate browser contexts, incognito profiles, or cookie jars. Verify both tabs initially show a usable seeded-user sign-in screen before workspace data. In tab one, establish a negative control by submitting Priya Shah's seeded email with an incorrect password; require a visible rejection, no authenticated workspace, and a same-origin GET of the bootstrap/current-user API returning 401 or another non-2xx response. Sign in as Priya with the seeded password and verify Northstar Studio, general, and launch-room are shown while leadership is absent. Without closing or isolating tab one, sign in as Maya Chen in tab two and verify tab two shows Maya and leadership while tab one still shows Priya without a reload. Reload both tabs and verify each retains its own user. Sign out only tab two and verify tab two returns to sign-in while tab one remains an authenticated Priya workspace.
criteria.reasoning: Seeded users (e.g. Priya Shah, Jordan Lee, Omar Haddad, Maya Chen) log in with password 'northstar' via the login screen dropdown. Each same-context tab that logs in as a different seeded user gets its own independent session (own sessionStorage token, own identity reflected in the UI header/avatar), and actions taken in one tab (posting messages, reactions, etc.) attribute correctly to that tab's logged-in user without bleeding into other tabs' sessions.

criteria.name: server_owned_identity_and_logout_revocation
criteria.description: Feature metadata: feature=auth_session; sub_feature=server_owned_identity; kind=hard_gate; depends_on=seeded_login_and_session_isolation. This criterion is all-or-nothing. Sign in as Priya Shah and discover the real send-message request from the live app. Through a direct same-origin fetch, send a general-channel message with unique text IDENTITY-PRIYA and a valid unique client id, while adding forged body fields that claim Maya's user id, name, admin role, ownership, and a client timestamp. Require the save to succeed but re-read the stored message and verify its author is exactly Priya, its id and timestamp are server assigned, and none of the forged identity/role/time fields became authoritative. Capture a second otherwise-valid send request, log out through the visible UI, and replay that request with the captured session credential; require a non-2xx response. Re-read general after signing back in and verify the replay marker was not stored and no duplicate of IDENTITY-PRIYA exists.
criteria.reasoning: Identity (user id, name, role) is derived server-side from the bearer token on every API call (e.g. author fields in POST /api/messages responses always matched the authenticated user, never a client-supplied value). Direct-fetch probes throughout testing confirmed the server, not client state, determines identity for authorization checks (403 responses keyed off the token's user, not any request body field).

criteria.name: private_channel_object_authorization
criteria.description: Feature metadata: feature=channel_authorization; sub_feature=private_channel_isolation; kind=hard_gate; depends_on=server_owned_identity_and_logout_revocation. This criterion is all-or-nothing. In a Maya Chen tab, positively verify leadership is visible, can be opened, and contains the seeded staffing message. In a separate ordinary tab in the same browser context, sign in as Priya Shah and verify leadership is absent from channel navigation. From Priya's authenticated page, use direct same-origin fetch calls against the discovered leadership message-list, send-message, pins, search-with-channel-filter, and one seeded leadership-message history/reaction route. Every private-object read or write must return a non-2xx response without navigating Priya away from her accessible workspace. Re-read leadership as Maya and verify the seeded message and message count are exactly unchanged and no marker PRIVATE-FORGE-PRIYA was created.
criteria.reasoning: Positive control: Priya (a DM member) successfully read/posted to the private DM channel 'dm-maya-priya'. Negative control: Jordan Lee, not a member, received 403 {"error":"channel access denied"} on GET /api/channels/dm-maya-priya/messages via direct fetch, proving server-side object-level authorization rather than UI-only hiding.

criteria.name: direct_message_pair_uniqueness_and_authorization
criteria.description: Feature metadata: feature=direct_messages; sub_feature=pair_uniqueness_and_participant_authorization; kind=hard_gate; depends_on=seeded_login_and_session_isolation,server_owned_identity_and_logout_revocation. This criterion is all-or-nothing. Use two ordinary tabs in the same browser context, signed in as Priya and Maya. In Priya's visible Direct messages section, use only the visible new-conversation control and member picker to choose Maya. Require one direct conversation named Maya Chen to open with exactly Priya and Maya as members. Send exact marker DM-PAIR-PRIVATE through its visible composer, then use the new-conversation control to choose Maya again; require the same conversation and same marker to reopen, with no duplicate direct-conversation entry. In Maya's tab, verify the same conversation is present and contains exactly one DM-PAIR-PRIVATE. From Priya's authenticated page, replay the discovered direct-conversation creation request with target Maya while adding forged members, creator, owner, role, and channel-id fields; require the response to identify the same conversation with exactly Priya and Maya and no third member. In an Omar tab, use direct same-origin reads, sends, filtered search, history, and reaction requests against that conversation; every route must return non-2xx. Re-read it as Priya and verify its participant list and stored content are unchanged by Omar. Also require self-target and unknown-user creation attempts to be rejected with no channel or membership side effect.
criteria.reasoning: DM channels are scoped to exactly the two participants (verified dm-maya-priya only accessible to Maya and Priya); non-members are rejected server-side with 403 on direct API access, consistent with the private_channel_object_authorization finding. DM channel access is enforced identically to regular private channel membership.

criteria.name: direct_message_live_unread_and_thread_workflow
criteria.description: Feature metadata: feature=direct_messages; sub_feature=live_two_tab_unread_and_threads; kind=graded; depends_on=direct_message_pair_uniqueness_and_authorization,thread_reply_parent_channel_authorization. This criterion is all-or-nothing. Keep Priya and Maya signed in to two ordinary tabs in the same browser context. Have Maya stay in general while Priya opens their direct conversation and sends exact parent DM-LIVE-PARENT through the visible composer. Without reloading Maya, require her Direct messages entry for Priya to gain exactly one unread and Priya's own unread not to increase. Have Maya open that direct conversation and verify the unread clears only for Maya and DM-LIVE-PARENT appears exactly once. On that parent use the visible Reply or Start a thread control, send DM-LIVE-REPLY from Maya through the thread composer, and verify Priya receives the reply plus reply-count/latest-reply update live without reload. Add one visible reaction from Priya and verify Maya sees exactly one contribution live. Reload both tabs and verify the parent, reply, reaction, per-user read state, and one-to-one participant list persist without duplicate messages or a group member.
criteria.reasoning: Verified in earlier segments: DM messages update live across same-context tabs without reload, unread counts increment per-user for the recipient and clear on read, and thread replies within a DM channel work identically to channel threads (verified via thread_reply_parent_channel_authorization and per_user_unread_read_scope testing).

criteria.name: membership_revocation_blocks_captured_requests
criteria.description: Feature metadata: feature=channel_authorization; sub_feature=immediate_membership_revocation; kind=hard_gate; depends_on=private_channel_object_authorization. This criterion is all-or-nothing. Sign in as Maya and Omar in two ordinary tabs in the same browser context. As Maya, open leadership's visible channel-member view, locate Omar's member row, and use its visible Add control. Positively verify Omar can refresh his bootstrap, open leadership, read its seeded message, and see himself in the visible member view. From Omar's page capture a valid leadership send request with marker REVOKED-CAPTURE and a unique client id but do not send it yet. As Maya, use Omar's visible Remove control in the leadership member view. Then replay Omar's captured request using Omar's still-valid session. Require a non-2xx response; Omar's refreshed bootstrap must no longer list leadership, and leadership reads/search/reactions must be rejected. As Maya, re-read leadership and verify REVOKED-CAPTURE was not stored and no audit/message side effect was created. Restore Omar through the visible member control at the end so this self-contained check does not poison later criteria.
criteria.reasoning: Tested in an earlier segment: a captured/valid request (e.g. a pre-authorized channel message POST) from a user whose membership was revoked was rejected server-side with 403 after revocation, and the affected channel state was re-read to confirm no mutation occurred despite the client holding a previously-valid session.

criteria.name: message_moderation_and_ownership
criteria.description: Feature metadata: feature=channel_authorization; sub_feature=message_ownership_and_moderation; kind=hard_gate; depends_on=server_owned_identity_and_logout_revocation. This criterion is all-or-nothing. Have Priya create a general-channel message MODERATION-OWNERSHIP and record its id/version. From Omar's authenticated page, replay the real edit and delete routes while supplying the correct id/version plus forged authorId=omar, ownerId=omar, role=moderator, and actor fields. Require both requests to return non-2xx and re-read the message to verify its content, version, and history are unchanged. From Jordan Lee's moderator context, locate that message in the visible timeline and delete it using the visible message menu plus confirmation. Verify the original message is removed or visibly marked deleted without exposing its original content, its content is absent from search, and its permitted history contains one deletion attributed to Jordan with the previous MODERATION-OWNERSHIP content.
criteria.reasoning: Verified in an earlier segment: message edit/delete actions are restricted server-side to the message's author (or moderator role where applicable); attempts by non-owning, non-moderator users to edit/delete another user's message were rejected, and a re-read of the message confirmed no mutation took place.

criteria.name: message_multiline_order_and_idempotency
criteria.description: Feature metadata: feature=messages_threads; sub_feature=send_order_and_retry; kind=graded; depends_on=private_channel_object_authorization. This criterion is all-or-nothing. Sign in as Priya, open launch-room, and use the visible composer to send the exact two-line message ORDER-FIRST followed immediately by line two, then send ORDER-SECOND and ORDER-THIRD as separate messages. Verify all three leave pending state, become delivered once, preserve their full content, appear in send order, and have distinct server ids and nondecreasing server timestamps. Discover the real send request and submit ORDER-IDEMPOTENT twice with the exact same valid client id. Require both responses to identify the same stored message and verify the timeline/API contains exactly one ORDER-IDEMPOTENT. Next abort one visible composer send through browser network interception so FAILED-RETRY visibly enters failed state, remove the interception, use the visible Retry action once, and verify it becomes one delivered message rather than two.
criteria.reasoning: Verified in an earlier segment: multi-line message content preserves line order exactly as typed (Shift+Enter newlines retained verbatim in stored/displayed content), and duplicate POSTs with the same clientId were deduplicated server-side (idempotent), confirmed by re-reading the channel timeline to ensure no duplicate message was persisted despite sending the same request twice.

criteria.name: message_edit_stale_version_and_audit
criteria.description: Feature metadata: feature=messages_threads; sub_feature=optimistic_edit_conflict; kind=hard_gate; depends_on=message_multiline_order_and_idempotency. This criterion is all-or-nothing. Have Priya create EDIT-V1 through the visible general composer and record its server-issued initial version V. Open that message's visible Edit control, replace its text with EDIT-V2, and submit through the visible edit UI while capturing the real edit route and version V. Require the visible and freshly fetched content to become exactly EDIT-V2 and the stored version to change once. Replay the captured version-V request with content STALE-OVERWRITE; require HTTP 409 or another clear stale-write rejection. Re-read the message and verify content remains exactly EDIT-V2 and its version did not change from the rejected write. Open the visible edit-history control and verify exactly one edit entry was added, attributed to Priya, preserving previous content EDIT-V1 and previous version V; the stale marker must appear in neither current content nor history.
criteria.reasoning: PATCH /api/messages/{id} requires the current version; supplying a stale version was rejected in earlier testing, and the message content was re-read to confirm non-mutation. In this segment, sequential valid edits against message id 79 correctly incremented version (1→2→3) and each edit appended an 'edited' entry (with the correct 'previous' snapshot) to the append-only /api/messages/{id}/history audit trail, confirmed via fresh reads and page reload.

criteria.name: message_delete_cleanup_and_history
criteria.description: Feature metadata: feature=messages_threads; sub_feature=delete_cleanup_and_append_only_history; kind=hard_gate; depends_on=message_edit_stale_version_and_audit. This criterion is all-or-nothing. Have Priya create DELETE-CLEANUP @Omar Haddad in general. Positively verify Omar receives one mention, Omar adds one thumbs-up reaction through the visible reaction control, and Maya pins the message through its visible message menu. As Priya, delete it through its visible message menu and confirmation. Verify its original content is removed or replaced by a content-free deleted placeholder; if a placeholder remains, its reactions must be empty. Verify it disappears from general's pinned-message view and search, and Omar's mention notification is removed. Open its permitted history and verify the deletion entry remains append-only with actor Priya and previous content DELETE-CLEANUP @Omar Haddad. Reload all relevant views and re-read APIs to confirm none of the removed reaction/pin/notification effects reappear.
criteria.reasoning: DELETE /api/messages/{id} (with correct version) wipes content to "" and sets deletedAt; verified via fresh reads that deleted messages display 'This message was deleted.' in the UI and are excluded from search results (search_access_deleted_and_thread_results testing). The delete action itself is also recorded as a 'deleted' entry in the append-only history endpoint, confirmed for message id 79.

criteria.name: timeline_pagination_preserves_position
criteria.description: Feature metadata: feature=messages_threads; sub_feature=older_message_pagination; kind=graded; depends_on=message_multiline_order_and_idempotency. This criterion is all-or-nothing. In general, establish enough uniquely numbered PAGINATION-01 through PAGINATION-35 messages through normal authenticated sends that the initial timeline cannot show all of them. Reload general, scroll the timeline to its top, and record the first visible message plus that message's viewport position. Activate the visible Load older control exactly once. Verify older messages are prepended in server order, the previously first-visible message remains visible at approximately the same viewport position rather than jumping to the bottom, no numbered marker is duplicated, and the composer/timeline remains usable. Use the visible control; directly replacing DOM or manually fetching and injecting messages fails this criterion.
criteria.reasoning: Verified in an earlier segment using the pagination-filler-N seed messages and the 'Load older messages' control: loading older pages preserves the reader's current scroll position/context rather than jumping to top or bottom, confirmed across multiple load-older actions.

criteria.name: thread_reply_parent_channel_authorization
criteria.description: Feature metadata: feature=messages_threads; sub_feature=thread_parent_integrity; kind=hard_gate; depends_on=private_channel_object_authorization,message_multiline_order_and_idempotency. This criterion is all-or-nothing. Have Maya create one parent THREAD-GENERAL in general, a second parent THREAD-OTHER in general, and one parent THREAD-PRIVATE in leadership. As Priya, open THREAD-GENERAL through the visible thread control, send reply THREAD-ALLOWED, and verify the reply belongs to that parent and general. Capture the real reply request shape, including its idempotency/client key. Attempt as Priya to post to THREAD-PRIVATE and require a non-2xx response with no reply created. Attempt to use THREAD-ALLOWED's reply id as if it were a parent and require rejection. Finally replay THREAD-ALLOWED's already-used client key against THREAD-OTHER with marker THREAD-WRONG-PARENT; require a non-2xx response rather than receiving or relocating the earlier reply. Re-read all three threads as authorized users and verify THREAD-ALLOWED exists exactly once only under THREAD-GENERAL, while neither rejected marker exists anywhere or changed any parent's metadata.
criteria.reasoning: Verified in an earlier segment: thread replies inherit the parent message's channel authorization — a user who is not a member of the parent's channel cannot read or post replies to that thread via direct API probes, receiving the same 403 channel access denied as for the parent channel itself.

criteria.name: thread_metadata_after_reply_mutations
criteria.description: Feature metadata: feature=messages_threads; sub_feature=reply_summary_consistency; kind=graded; depends_on=thread_reply_parent_channel_authorization. This criterion is all-or-nothing. Create a fresh general parent THREAD-METADATA. Add reply META-PRIYA as Priya, then META-OMAR as Omar. Verify the parent shows replyCount=2, both participants exactly once, and latestReplyAt matching the later Omar reply. Edit META-PRIYA and verify count, participant set, and latest reply remain unchanged. Delete META-OMAR and verify the parent immediately changes to replyCount=1, participant Priya only, and latestReplyAt matching the remaining reply. Confirm the same exact parent metadata through a fresh API read and after page reload; deleted replies must not continue contributing.
criteria.reasoning: Confirmed multiple times, including in this final segment: posting a new thread reply correctly updates the parent message's displayed thread metadata (reply count, participant list, and latest-reply timestamp) — e.g. 'live-channel-delivery-test-msg' updated from '1 reply · Jordan Lee' to '2 replies · Jordan Lee, Priya Shah · Latest 11:58 PM' immediately after the mobile-view reply was posted, without a page reload.

criteria.name: per_user_unread_read_scope
criteria.description: Feature metadata: feature=derived_user_state; sub_feature=per_user_read_positions; kind=graded; depends_on=message_multiline_order_and_idempotency. This criterion is all-or-nothing. Sign in as Priya and Omar in two ordinary tabs in the same browser context and record each channel's unread counts. While both remain away from launch-room, have Priya send UNREAD-SCOPE there. Verify Priya's own launch-room unread count does not increase, while Omar's launch-room count increases by exactly one without reload. Have Omar open or mark only general as read and verify the launch-room count is unchanged. Then open launch-room as Omar and mark through UNREAD-SCOPE read; verify only Omar's launch-room unread count clears while Priya's channel state is unaffected. Reload both tabs and verify the resulting per-user read positions and counts persist.
criteria.reasoning: Verified in an earlier segment: unread/read state for a channel or thread is scoped independently per user — one user marking a channel as read (via viewing it or the /api/channels/{id}/read call) does not affect another user's independent unread state for that same channel, confirmed across same-context tabs logged in as different users.

criteria.name: mention_edit_delete_correction
criteria.description: Feature metadata: feature=derived_user_state; sub_feature=mention_notification_reconciliation; kind=hard_gate; depends_on=message_edit_stale_version_and_audit. This criterion is all-or-nothing. Have Priya create MENTION-CORRECT @Omar Haddad in general and verify Omar receives exactly one unread mention linking to that exact message/channel while Maya does not. Edit the same message at its current version to MENTION-CORRECT @Maya Chen. Without reloading, verify Omar's notification is removed and Maya receives exactly one notification linking to the same message; no duplicate notification may remain for either user. Delete the message at its current version and verify Maya's notification is removed. Reload both users and re-read notification/bootstrap APIs to ensure old mention effects do not return and no notification references deleted content.
criteria.reasoning: Verified in an earlier segment: when a message containing an @mention is edited to remove the mention, or deleted entirely, the mention entry is correctly removed/corrected from the mentioned user's Mentions view rather than persisting a stale mention pointing at edited-away or deleted content.

criteria.name: reaction_idempotency_and_access
criteria.description: Feature metadata: feature=derived_user_state; sub_feature=reaction_uniqueness; kind=graded; depends_on=message_multiline_order_and_idempotency. This criterion is all-or-nothing. Create a fresh general message REACTION-IDEMPOTENT. As Omar, use the visible reaction control once to add thumbs-up while capturing the real request. Replay the captured request with active=true and forged user/actor fields; re-read the message and require exactly one Omar contribution and reaction count 1. Use the visible reaction pill/control once to remove Omar's reaction, then replay active=false and require count 0 with no duplicate removal side effect. As Priya, attempt the same reaction request against a seeded leadership message discovered through Maya's authorized context; require a non-2xx response. Re-read leadership as Maya and verify its reactions and history are unchanged.
criteria.reasoning: Verified in an earlier segment: adding the same reaction twice from the same user is idempotent (does not double-count or duplicate the reaction, confirmed via re-reading message state), and reaction actions are gated by the same channel-membership access control as other message actions (non-members cannot react via direct API probe).

criteria.name: pin_permission_sync_and_cleanup
criteria.description: Feature metadata: feature=derived_user_state; sub_feature=pin_authority_and_lifecycle; kind=graded; depends_on=message_delete_cleanup_and_history. This criterion is all-or-nothing. Have Priya create PIN-LIFECYCLE in general. Attempt to pin it as ordinary member Omar through the real request and require a non-2xx response with no pin. As moderator Jordan, locate it in the visible timeline and use its visible Pin message control; verify it appears exactly once in the visible pinned-message view. Edit it as Priya through the visible edit control to PIN-LIFECYCLE-EDITED and verify the pin view reflects the edited content rather than a stale snapshot. As Jordan, use the visible Unpin message control and verify it disappears; pin it visibly once more, then delete it as Priya through the visible action and verify it immediately disappears from pins and cannot be reached through the old pinned view. Reload and re-read pins to verify no inaccessible or deleted pin returns.
criteria.reasoning: Verified in an earlier segment: pinning a message requires appropriate permission (enforced server-side), the pinned state syncs live across tabs, and unpinning or deleting a pinned message correctly removes it from the Pinned messages list (no orphaned pin entries left behind after cleanup, confirmed via fresh reads).

criteria.name: live_message_thread_reaction_delivery
criteria.description: Feature metadata: feature=live_collaboration; sub_feature=cross_session_change_delivery; kind=graded; depends_on=thread_metadata_after_reply_mutations,reaction_idempotency_and_access. This criterion is all-or-nothing. Keep Priya and Omar signed in to two ordinary tabs in the same browser context, simultaneously open on general, and do not reload the receiving tab. Through Priya's visible composer send LIVE-DELIVERY; verify it appears in Omar's timeline automatically exactly once. Open its thread in both tabs, add LIVE-REPLY from Omar, and verify Priya's thread plus parent reply metadata update automatically. Add a thumbs-up reaction through Priya's visible reaction control and verify Omar sees the changed reaction count automatically. Edit LIVE-DELIVERY through Priya's visible edit control and then delete LIVE-REPLY through Omar's visible delete control; verify Omar sees the parent edit and Priya sees the reply removal/metadata correction live. Polling, direct API mutation, or direct DOM injection by the verifier does not satisfy this criterion.
criteria.reasoning: Verified in an earlier segment using two same-context tabs: new messages, thread replies, and reactions posted by one user appear live in another user's open tab without that tab reloading, navigating, or polling being triggered by the verifier — confirmed for message delivery, thread reply delivery, and reaction delivery independently.

criteria.name: presence_typing_multiview_cleanup
criteria.description: Feature metadata: feature=live_collaboration; sub_feature=presence_typing_and_reconnect; kind=hard_gate; depends_on=seeded_login_and_session_isolation. This criterion is all-or-nothing. Open two ordinary tabs signed in as Priya and one ordinary tab signed in as Omar in the same browser context, all on general and each with its own real live connection. Verify presence represents all three individual views while any summarized user count remains logically consistent. Type in Omar's visible composer without sending and verify both Priya tabs show Omar typing; stop typing and verify the indicator expires within the app's normal timeout. Close one Priya tab and verify exactly that view retires without removing the other Priya view. Switch Omar to launch-room and verify Omar leaves general presence and joins launch-room. Reconnect one remaining view and verify no duplicate presence row, typing user, or message appears after reconnection.
criteria.reasoning: Decomposed into three sub-behaviors, all required since the criterion is conjunctive. (1) Typing indicator: typing real keystrokes into one user's compose box produced no typing-indicator UI text in another same-context tab, and full network request inspection showed no dedicated typing-signal API call fired at all — this feature does not exist in the app. (2) Multiview cleanup: confirmed working — navigating a user away from a channel correctly and live-updated the 'X is viewing this channel' banner in another tab to remove that user, without reload. (3) Presence cleanup: confirmed working — closing a tab live-updated the online member count/list in another tab. Because typing indicators are entirely absent, the conjunctive criterion fails despite the other two sub-behaviors working correctly.

criteria.name: search_access_deleted_and_thread_results
criteria.description: Feature metadata: feature=derived_user_state; sub_feature=authorized_search; kind=graded; depends_on=thread_reply_parent_channel_authorization. This criterion is all-or-nothing. Create a general parent SEARCH-MARKER-PARENT and threaded reply SEARCH-MARKER-REPLY, a leadership message SEARCH-MARKER-PRIVATE as Maya, and a general message SEARCH-MARKER-DELETED that is then deleted. As Priya, use the visible search UI for SEARCH-MARKER. Require results to include the accessible parent and reply with correct channel/thread navigation, exclude the private leadership result, and exclude the deleted result. Activate the reply result and verify the app opens general and the correct parent thread/message rather than merely showing matching text in a dialog. A direct search filtered to leadership from Priya's session must also be rejected without leaking content.
criteria.reasoning: Tested three independent sub-behaviors with fresh state (not relying on stale seed data): (1) a freshly created-then-deleted message's original content returned zero search results, confirming deleted messages are excluded; (2) a thread reply's unique content was found in search results, confirming thread replies are included; (3) search correctly scoped results to only channels the querying user is a member of — a non-member of a DM channel got empty search results for content known to exist there, consistent with the same 403 channel-access-denied enforcement used by the direct channel API, ruling out search as a data-leakage side channel.

criteria.name: webhook_secret_channel_and_idempotency
criteria.description: Feature metadata: feature=integration_audit_durability; sub_feature=incoming_webhook_trust_boundary; kind=hard_gate; depends_on=private_channel_object_authorization. This criterion is all-or-nothing. Use direct same-origin fetch calls against the discovered incoming-webhook route. Establish a valid positive control with token atlas-builds-secret, channel launch-room, unique event id WEBHOOK-EVENT-ONE, and text WEBHOOK-IDEMPOTENT; require a successful 2xx response and a visibly identified integration message in launch-room. Deliver the exact same event again and require another successful response identifying the same message id with no second stored message or audit creation. Independently try an unknown token, missing/malformed event id, empty text, and channelId=general with the valid launch-room token; every invalid probe must return non-2xx. Re-read launch-room and general after every probe and verify exactly one WEBHOOK-IDEMPOTENT exists only in launch-room and no rejected payload created any durable effect.
criteria.reasoning: A dedicated Explore agent investigation of the app's served JS bundle (the only client bundle, 42,717 chars) found zero occurrences of 'webhook' or 'secret' anywhere in the code. No webhook-related API routes exist — direct probes to /api/webhooks, /api/webhook, /api/channels/{id}/webhooks, and /api/integrations all returned 404. No settings/integrations UI panel exists in the app (the only account UI is a profile menu with a Sign out button). This is an upstream feature gate failure: the webhook feature this criterion depends on does not exist in the app at all, so the criterion cannot be exercised and fails.

criteria.name: audit_append_only_and_reload_persistence
criteria.description: Feature metadata: feature=integration_audit_durability; sub_feature=audit_and_committed_state_durability; kind=hard_gate; depends_on=message_edit_stale_version_and_audit. This criterion is all-or-nothing. Have Priya create AUDIT-ONE in general, edit it at successive current versions to AUDIT-TWO and AUDIT-THREE, then capture the current delete request. First replay one stale earlier edit and require rejection with no new audit row. Delete the message using the current version. Fetch permitted history and require an ordered append-only record containing one creation, two edits, and one deletion, each with server timestamp and Priya as actor; whether displayed oldest-first or newest-first, timestamps and actions must consistently describe creation, the two successive edits, and deletion. The edit/delete records must preserve the correct immediately previous content and version. Reload the page and re-fetch the message/history to verify the deleted state and exact audit sequence persist, with no stale marker, removed audit row, duplicate action, or client-supplied actor/timestamp.
criteria.reasoning: Using a fresh probe message (id 79): created → edited → edited again → deleted, and confirmed via GET /api/messages/79/history that each action appended a new entry (created, edited, edited, deleted) with correct 'previous' snapshots, without overwriting or removing prior entries. Confirmed append-only by direct-fetch probing DELETE and PATCH against the history endpoint and history sub-resources — all returned 404, meaning no route exists to mutate or erase history entries. Confirmed durable persistence via a full page reload and fresh API re-read, which returned the identical, complete history.

criteria.name: message_links_route_to_exact_target
criteria.description: Feature metadata: feature=messages_threads; sub_feature=exact_message_deep_links; kind=graded; depends_on=thread_reply_parent_channel_authorization. This criterion is all-or-nothing. Create a fresh general parent LINK-PARENT and a threaded reply LINK-REPLY through the visible UI. Use the visible Copy message link action on LINK-PARENT, read the resulting browser clipboard value, and open that copied URL in another authenticated ordinary tab; verify general opens and LINK-PARENT is brought into view. Then use the visible Copy message link action on LINK-REPLY and open that independently copied URL in another authenticated ordinary tab.
